title: Head-on situation: which way do you turn? COLREG Rule 14 explained
description: COLREG Rule 14 in 3D: two power-driven vessels meeting on reciprocal courses. Both alter course to starboard and pass port to port. What you see by night and what to do when in doubt.

source.title: Convention on the International Regulations for Preventing Collisions at Sea, 1972 (COLREG)

script: Two power-driven vessels are meeting head-on. Which way do you turn? You see a vessel ahead, on a reciprocal course. By night you see both her sidelights, and her masthead lights in a line. Rule 14 is clear: each vessel alters course to starboard, so that they pass port to port. In a head-on situation there is no stand-on vessel. Both must act. If you are in any doubt whether the situation exists, assume that it does. And make your alteration large and early, with one short blast. Head-on means alter to starboard, and pass port to port.
